root_cause.text: The vsock core’s `vsock_update_buffer_size()` applied buffer-size clamps in the wrong order, so when `vsk->buffer_min_size` exceeded `vsk->buffer_max_size` the later minimum clamp overrode the maximum limit and let `vsk->buffer_size` exceed its intended upper bound.
root_cause.evidence: The patch in `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c` moves the `if (val > vsk->buffer_max_size)` check to occur after `if (val < vsk->buffer_min_size)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that clamping to maximum first and then minimum “inverted the constraint” and allowed `vsk->buffer_size` to grow beyond `vsk->buffer_max_size`.
